summary: Allowed arrival intervals for starting the job; early arrival waits, lateness beyond max_visit_lateness is infeasible.
range: Array of [start,end] Unix-second pairs; each start <= end. Overlapping windows are allowed (solver may use any).
constraints: Each [start,end] with start <= end; non-negative Unix seconds (C2).
businessRules: Arrival must land in a window (or within max_visit_lateness); early arrival waits and inflates duration (C2).
Overlapping windows on a job are permitted — the solver may use any; feasible arrival is in their union (C2 edge case).

time_windows defines: Define time periods within which this job should be started. The time periods should be expressed as a UNIX timestamp in seconds. Please note that the time periods should not overlap with each othe…
Each element in time_windows must be valid and consistent with related fields.
Must stay consistent with: vehicles.time_window, jobs.max_visit_lateness, jobs.service. Changes here may require validation of those fields.
Rule: Higher priority jobs are serviced first; ties break by job ID order.
Rule: Shipments: pickup always occurs before delivery on the route.
Optional field. Omitting uses solver's default behavior (no penalty).
validationRules: A window with end < start -> 400 input validation failed (C2: start <= end; API Facts §4).
testingGuidance: Positive: window [36000,43200]; vehicle can arrive 09:40 -> waits to 10:00 then services (C2 example 1).
Positive: a job with overlapping windows -> solver may use any; feasible arrival in the union (C2 edge case).
Boundary: instant window [t,t] -> must arrive exactly at t (or within max_visit_lateness) (C2 edge case).
Negative-validation: a window with end < start -> 400 (C2).
Negative-infeasible: window ends before the earliest possible arrival with max_visit_lateness 0 -> unassigned (time-window reason) (C2 example 2).
Interaction: a long wait for a late window inflates elapsed time and can breach the shift / max_travel_time -> unassigned (C2+C6).
Interaction: Combination: tight capacity + one high-priority + one low-priority job competing for the last slot -> high-priority assigned, low-priority unassigned.
Interaction: Combination: high-priority job whose only skill is unavailable on any vehicle -> still unassigned despite priority.
Interaction: Interaction: two jobs with equal priority; one has outsourcing_cost 100, other 50 -> cost-based job assigned first.
Interaction: Infeasible: job window [09:00,09:30], max_visit_lateness 0, nearest vehicle arrives 09:45 -> unassigned.
Interaction: Interaction: a long wait for a late window pushes route end past the shift -> unassigned (couples with max-duration-distance-cap).
Interaction: Shipment: delivery window [09:00,09:30], max_visit_lateness 15, nearest vehicle arrives 09:40 -> accepted within lateness.
Interaction: Break: break time_windows [12:00,13:00], vehicle arrives 12:30 -> break scheduled at 12:30.
